title: Keep report renders from stalling the other requests

blocks.text: The reporting service moved to virtual threads last month: the web server now runs every request on a virtual thread of its own and calls `ReportService.handle(...)` there. Since then, whenever finance pulls a batch of quarterly reports, the service's liveness probe times out, the orchestrator restarts the instance, and ordinary requests that render nothing see their latency jump. Rendering a report is pure computation, with no I/O: the `Renderer` you are given takes tens to hundreds of milliseconds of CPU per report.

items: `render(reportId)`: produces one report for the calling request.

blocks.text: When you're done, a batch of reports can no longer hold up the service's other requests, rendering never uses more than the `cores` the service was given, and when that many reports are requested together, they all render at once. About two lines in total.
The tests send each request on a virtual thread of its own, as the web server does, and hold renders in progress to see where and how many run at once.

cases.says: six requests made at once each get back the report they asked for
no report is rendered on a virtual thread
with two cores set aside for rendering, no more than two reports render at once, however many are requested
with three cores set aside for rendering, three reports requested together render at the same time

origin.section: A Virtual Thread That Computes Keeps Its Carrier: Java 21 Has No Time Slice

concepts: CPU-heavy work goes to a platform pool sized to the cores, and the virtual thread waits for its result, which frees the carrier.
